persona.bio: Mia, 31, social media manager at a fitness apparel brand. She lives in Canva: every post, story and ad is built there, and she uses Canva's AI features most days. She uses ChatGPT every day for captions and hooks, plans the content calendar in Notion, schedules in Later, answers comments and DMs, writes briefs for creators by email in Gmail, and pulls weekly numbers into Google Sheets. Her company encourages AI and she may connect her work Gmail.

path.role: You’re a social media manager at a fitness apparel brand, running everything through Canva and the main social platforms.

steps.note: I am a social media manager at a fitness apparel brand. I write captions, comment replies and short emails for our followers and customers. My tone is warm, upbeat and direct, like a friend who runs. I keep captions short, with a strong first line that leads with how something feels, not a sales pitch. Replies are one or two sentences. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, sizes, fabrics, dates or discount codes. Use a square bracket where something is missing. Do not use hype or pushy words. Give me a draft I can read and edit before anything goes out.

steps.title: Your captions, with a saved assistant
steps.read: Your captions now come from a saved assistant in ChatGPT that already knows your brand voice. You hand it the product and the angle, and it drafts in your words and waits for you to read it. That beats starting from scratch many times a day, because the tone stays the same from post to post.

material.label: Instructions for your assistant
items: You are my caption writer. I am a social media manager at a fitness apparel brand, and I post on Instagram and TikTok many times a day. Write captions in my voice: warm, upbeat and direct, like a friend who runs. Start with a strong first line that leads with how the piece feels while moving, never with a sales pitch. Keep captions short, usually two to four lines, and end with a simple call to action only when I ask for one. Avoid hype words, pushy language and filler. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, fabrics, sizes, dates or discount codes. Put a square bracket where something is missing. When I describe a post, give me three caption options and one alternative first line for each. I will read and edit everything before it goes out.

material.label: Examples to start with
items:
Request: Swap the hook on the leggings post. Make it less salesy and lead with how they feel on a run.
Caption: Mile three and you forget you are even wearing them. Our [product name] move with you, not against you. Tell us where your next run is taking you.

Request: Caption for a new sports bra photo, relaxed tone.
Caption: Built for the days you want to move and not think about it. [Product name] is here. Which workout are you saving it for?

Request: Short caption for a behind the scenes video of the team testing gear.
Caption: We tested it the only way we know how: by sweating in it. Watch the team put [product name] through a full session.

steps.title: Your comment replies, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your common comment replies now live on your phone’s keyboard. You type a few letters and the full reply appears, then you change a name or a detail and send it. That keeps your answers friendly and consistent, and you still read every one before it goes.

material.label: Your replies
items: Thank you so much, [first name]! We are so glad you love it. Tell us how your next workout goes!
Great question, [first name]! [Answer from your approved info]. Let us know if you need anything else.
We are so sorry about that, [first name]. Please send us a message with your order details and we will make it right.
Thanks for the love, [first name]! We will pass it along to the team.
Good news, [first name]! [Product name] is available in [sizes or colors]. Check the link in our bio for the latest.
Hi [first name], thanks for asking! We do not have an update on that yet, but follow along and you will be the first to know.
Love seeing this, [first name]! Tag us in your next workout so we can see it.

safeUse: Never type customer names, addresses, order numbers or email addresses into ChatGPT. Use square brackets instead.
Keep unreleased products, launch dates and pricing out of the chat unless your company has approved it.
Do not paste private messages or comments that show a follower’s personal details.
Read every caption and reply before it goes out, and check product facts against your own approved info.
Never let a draft promise discounts, sizes or shipping that you have not confirmed.
steps.askMessage: Hi [manager name], I would like to confirm which AI tools are approved for my work and what I may use them for. I am planning to use ChatGPT to draft captions and replies to comments, and possibly emails and content calendar ideas. I would not enter customer names, order details or unreleased product information, and I would read everything before it goes out. Could you let me know what is approved, and whether linking my work email to an AI tool is okay?

design.today: You write captions many times a day, often from scratch each time. A request like swapping the hook on the leggings post comes in with a deadline of 3.
design.newWay: A saved assistant in ChatGPT knows your brand voice and how your captions are built, so you give it the product and the angle and it drafts a few options. You say the angle out loud or paste the request, and it writes the hook and caption. Every caption comes back in a form you can paste straight into Canva or Later, and you pick, tweak and post. Your voice stays the same across posts and you stop starting from a blank page.

steps.goal: Collect five to ten of your best past captions and note what makes each one sound like your brand.
Get ChatGPT ready on both your phone and your computer.
Save a short description of your role and brand tone so every chat starts with it.
Make a project for captions and add your past captions and tone notes to it.
Set up the saved caption assistant so you can give it a product and an angle and get a few hook options back.
Try it on the leggings request about a less salesy hook that leads with how they feel on a run, and adjust the instructions until it sounds like you.

material.label: Brand voice notes
material.what: How your brand sounds, words you use and words you avoid, in a few short lines.

material.label: Caption assistant instructions
material.what: Tells the assistant to write a hook, a body and a call to action from a product and an angle, and to give three options.

material.label: Example captions
material.what: Your best past captions, so the assistant copies your style and not a generic one.

material.label: Hook swap request
material.what: A ready prompt for requests like swapping a hook, with space for the post, the angle and the platform.

design.checkPoint: You read every caption and check product names, claims and links before you paste it into Canva or Later and post.

design.today: You reply to comments many times a day, one at a time.
design.newWay: Your most common replies are written once in your brand voice and kept ready, so a sizing, shipping or restock comment gets an answer in seconds. For comments that need some thought, you paste the comment into your saved ChatGPT project and get a draft that sounds like you. You still read and post each reply yourself, so it stays personal and you are not typing the same answer all day.

steps.goal: List the ten comments you get most often, such as sizing, shipping, restocks and colors, and write down your usual answer to each.
Make a project for comment replies and add your usual answers and tone notes.
Set up an assistant that turns a pasted comment into a short reply in your voice, using your usual answers where they fit.
Save your ten most common replies on your phone so each is a few letters away when you answer on the go.
Run a week of real comments through it and add any new question that keeps coming up to your list.

material.label: Common replies
material.what: Your ten most frequent comment answers, written short and in your voice.

material.label: Comment reply instructions
material.what: Tells the assistant to answer briefly and warmly, use your usual answers, and flag anything it cannot answer.

material.label: Tricky comment guide
material.what: How you want complaints, sizing problems and unclear questions handled, such as moving them to a direct message.

material.label: Keyboard shortcuts list
material.what: The short letter codes for each saved reply so you can find them fast.

design.checkPoint: You read every reply before you post it, and you answer complaints and anything about orders yourself.
